recognize_zh: 藍色背景中，多顆梭形到卵圓形細胞的胞質顆粒呈紫紅色的變色反應（metachromasia），這是甲苯胺藍（toluidine blue）染色下肥大細胞的特徵；圖中另見黃綠色含鐵血黃素顆粒。
features: Numerous spindled to ovoid cells with metachromatic purple-magenta cytoplasmic granules
Granule intensity varies; some cells hypogranular with only faint purple staining
Oval bland nuclei; cells arranged in a loose streaming lesion
Scattered yellow-green refractile granules consistent with hemosiderin
Background orthochromatic blue-stained hematopoietic cells and fat spaces
describe_en: Toluidine blue (or Giemsa-type) stain on a bone marrow biopsy highlights a loose lesion of spindled to ovoid cells containing metachromatic purple cytoplasmic granules, with variable degranulation or hypogranularity in a subset. Scattered yellow-green hemosiderin granules are present. The remaining hematopoietic cells stain orthochromatically blue. Findings are consistent with a mast cell infiltrate of systemic mastocytosis; because hypogranular neoplastic mast cells may be underestimated by metachromatic stains, tryptase and CD25 immunostains are preferred for quantification.

ddx.vs: Basophils are round with segmented nuclei and are 2D7/BB1-positive and CD25-negative, not spindled lesion-forming cells.
Reactive mast cells are round, scattered singly and well granulated rather than forming spindled aggregates.
Macrophage pigment is golden-green and refractile, not metachromatic purple, and stains blue with Prussian blue.
